id.description: Stable, protocol-neutral action identifier in reverse-DNS-like dot-separated lowercase segments. It identifies meaning only, never a runtime target.

version.description: Explicit positive integer contract version. Runtime bindings reference action ID plus this version (D-013).

title.description: Human-readable short label for the action, suitable for any surface projection.

description.description: One clear statement of what the action does. Untrusted runtime content must not be embedded here (it becomes tool metadata).

inputSchema.description: JSON Schema for caller input only. Trusted context (actor, tenant, current record, current selection, confirmation) is resolved by the runtime and never enters this schema.

outputSchema.description: Optional JSON Schema describing the action's successful output; null when unstructured.

scope.description: Where the action's meaning/executability depends on context. `portable`: semantics are not intrinsically dependent on a particular UI or agent surface; execution still requires a compatible runtime binding and all required trusted context. `page_scoped`: depends on the active page/application surface. `browser_local`: local to browser/UI state, may have no server equivalent. `headless`: intended for non-visual runtimes.

effect.description: Observable state change execution can cause. Effect is not risk. `read`: no state change. `reversible_write`: restorable change. `destructive_write`: non-restorable change. `external_side_effect`: change outside this application's transactional reach.

risk.description: Level of user/business consequence. `low`, `moderate`, and `high` form an ordinal review scale. `consequential` is a categorical gate, not an ordinal step: execution requires a runtime-issued, opaque confirmation receipt and must not be compared ordinally with the other values. Risk is orthogonal to effect.

idempotency.description: Server-side deduplication policy. `none`: no deduplication. `recommended_key`: deduplicates when a caller supplies a key; proceeds without one otherwise. `required_key`: invocation without a valid key is rejected before execution.

outputSensitivity.description: Confidentiality classification of the action's output. Controls output policy/redaction handling (e.g. `sensitive` output is subject to redaction and must not be assumed safe for agent surfaces). Independent of `outputContentTrust`: an output may be `sensitive` AND contain untrusted content simultaneously; neither dimension suppresses the other (D-032).

outputContentTrust.description: Whether downstream agent consumers must treat the action's output as untrusted content. `contains_untrusted_content` requires surfaces to apply untrusted-content handling (e.g. WebMCP untrustedContentHint); it is independent of `outputSensitivity` — `sensitive` output may also contain untrusted content (D-032).

contextRequirements.description: Trusted facts the runtime must resolve before invocation. These come exclusively from trusted runtime context (authenticated sources, request state, UI runtime), never from caller input. `human_confirmation` is necessary but not sufficient for consequential actions: authority comes only from a runtime-issued confirmation receipt.

extensions.description: Namespaced extension point for adapter/driver metadata. Keys must be of the form `namespace/key`; runtime binding details belong in RuntimeBinding, not here.
